analysis:
The PR is documentation-only. It touches docs/provider/cli-reference.md in two places: the "Last updated" date (line 3) and a new `darkbloom status` bullet at head lines 990-1001. The bullet describes a "Requests served since the daemon started" counter, implemented in StatusCommand+ServedRequests.swift. It says the counter covers finished coordinator requests, counts output tokens only, resets on daemon restart or when an availability window opens, includes requests that ended early on a coordinator cancel or dropped connection, and includes free self-route requests. It also links to an immutable platform commit for the heartbeat cumulativeDelta logic.

I saw no change to a security control, trust boundary, key handling, attestation, authorization, encryption or prefix-cache behavior. Nothing in the doc changes the retained T-041 posture, which concerns the SSD cache TTL, HMAC names and SEC-035.

The new status text exposes only aggregate counters to the local operator through a local CLI. It exposes no prompt content, no request IDs and no keys. Its statement that the coordinator may not pay for early-ended requests is operator-facing information about billing semantics; it is not itself a billing control.

The actual Swift implementation and the platform heartbeat code are outside the supplied evidence. I cannot verify that the doc matches that code, for example that the counter contains no per-consumer data. I raise no finding for that unverified contract. The doc change itself introduces no concrete regression.
